extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners before the USPTO, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and legal professionals interested in USPTO disciplinary procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing imposition of reciprocal discipline by the USPTO when a practitioner has been disciplined by a state authority, including notice, response period, suspension terms, restitution, publication, notifications, and reinstatement procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline procedure (37 C.F.R. § 11.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, a Notice and Order notifies the respondent that the OED Director has filed a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline requesting imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to discipline imposed by a state court; the respondent is provided an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the respondent receives the Notice and Order and does not file a response within the 40-day period, the OED may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and impose the reciprocal discipline. The Notice should be served (here, by certified mail) and include reference to the state action and the basis for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for reciprocal discipline: state discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's reciprocal discipline is predicated on his violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), having been disciplined by a duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A practitioner's suspension or other discipline by a state authority can serve as the predicate for identical or reciprocal discipline by the USPTO under the cited federal regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension terms and restitution as conditions of discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the USPTO for three (3) years and until Respondent pays restitution in the amount of $750 to Ressie Holmes; $1,500 to Beth Griffin; and $1,090 to Derrick Plummer and Gwenevere Plummer Scales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The period of suspension and monetary restitution amounts are enforceable conditions; suspension remains in effect until restitution is paid and any reinstatement requirements are satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement petition requirement (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall remain suspended from practice before the USPTO until the OED Director grants a petition requesting Respondent's reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement is not automatic at the end of the suspension period; the respondent must petition the OED Director under the regulatory procedure set out in § 11.60 and obtain OED approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication requirement: Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette containing: the respondent's name and registration number; the fact and duration of suspension; restitution amounts; the statutory/regulatory basis for discipline (e.g., 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)); the underlying state court order and basis (e.g., findings of neglected client matters, misrepresentations, failure to return unearned fees); and where disciplinary decisions are available for public review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order includes a template Notice of Suspension that summarizes the facts, rules violated, disciplinary terms, and where to find the full decisions (OED FOIA Reading Room URL). The Gazette notice informs the public and the bar of the discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where the respondent is admitted to practice, to courts where the respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED must proactively notify relevant state agencies and courts of USPTO disciplinary actions, ensuring reciprocal awareness among jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of suspended practitioners (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the Order does not restate § 11.58 duties, it imposes the regulatory obligations that suspended practitioners must follow (e.g., notifications to clients, ceasing practice before the USPTO, handling of files), and requires compliance with those enumerated duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO Customer Numbers and verified Electronic System accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall dissociate Respondent's name from any Customer Number(s) and USPTO verified Electronic System account(s), if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative action will be taken to remove the respondent's association with online filing/customer identifiers to prevent continuing practice via those credentials during suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obtaining or being added to a USPTO Customer Number until reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for a USPTO Customer Number, shall not obtain a USPTO Customer Number, nor shall he have his name added to a USPTO Customer Number, unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explicitly prevents a suspended practitioner from re-entering USPTO electronic practice indirectly through new or shared customer numbers until formal reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: State professional-conduct rule violations as factual predicates
rubrics_metrics.description: The Illinois Supreme Court's January 29, 2019 Order was based on a Report stating that Mr. Davis 'neglected three client matters and failed to properly communicate and return unearned fees with respect to four client matters,' 'made misrepresentations regarding what work he performed with respect to one client matter,' and 'failed to cooperate in disciplinary investigations.' The December 18, 2017 Complaint alleged violations of Illinois Rules 1.3, 1.4(a)(3), 1.4(a)(4), 1.16(d), 8.1(b), and 8.4(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Findings of neglect, poor communication, failure to return unearned fees, misrepresentation about work performed, and failure to cooperate with investigations are classic bases for state discipline and thus for reciprocal USPTO discipline when adopted by the state tribunal. The Order cites both the factual findings and the specific Illinois Rule numbers used to justify discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service by certified mail with tracking
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order was sent by certified mail (receipt nos. ... ) notifying Respondent that the OED Director had filed a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper service of a disciplinary notice is effected via certified mail with receipt tracking; record of service is included in the administrative file and is relevant to calculating response deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority for USPTO discipline (35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24; disciplinary decisions are available for public review at the OED FOIA Reading Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary actions rest on federal statute and USPTO regulations; the Order cites the legal basis and provides the public access point for full disciplinary decisions.
